additional_requirements: Symptoms must develop within 3 months of the onset of the stressor
Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

info.persona: Brian Keller merges a precise, data‑centric mind with a solitary, artistic soul, turning inventory spreadsheets into canvas‑inspired efficiencies while nurturing a quiet habit of solving puzzles and tending herb jars in a world that often feels too noisy.
info.professional_persona: Brian Keller, a methodical inventory control specialist at a bustling Bronx distribution center, blends their expertise in SAP WM, advanced Excel analytics, and barcode scanning with an imaginative flair to redesign warehouse layouts that cut pick times while integrating subtle artistic touches.
info.cultural_background: Brian is a white American of mixed Irish and German ancestry who grew up in a middle‑class family in the Bronx, New York. He attended a public high school and completed some college coursework at a community college before entering the logistics field. Living in the culturally diverse Bronx has exposed him to a rich tapestry of cuisines, street art, and community festivals, which he appreciates but balances with his preference for quieter, solitary environments. His upbringing emphasized hard work, community harmony, and respect for individual space, shaping his polite, cooperative demeanor and his appreciation for both American and broader Western cultural values.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Brian prefers solitary, reflective pursuits. He enjoys sketching and digital illustration, exploring abstract and modern art, and reading science‑fiction novels. He listens to ambient and instrumental music while working on personal projects. Weekends often find him solving puzzles such as crosswords and Sudoku, tending to a small indoor herb garden, and experimenting with Python scripts to automate routine inventory tasks. He also frequents quiet coffee shops and local museums to read, sketch, and absorb the artistic atmosphere of the Bronx.
info.sports_persona: Brian Keller, a quiet supporter of the Bronx‑based New York Yankees and a fan of the New York Knicks, curls up on weekends to jog solo along the Bronx River Greenway, participates in a local adult recreational basketball league at the Bronx Community Center, and practices a minimalist yoga routine to offset back pain, deliberately avoiding crowded gyms to preserve their love of solitude.
info.arts_persona: Brian Keller, an avid sketcher and digital illustrator, spends afternoons at the Bronx Museum of the Arts studying works by Piet Mondrian and Yayoi Kusama, draws inspiration from ambient composers Brian Eno and Max Richter, and fills sketchbooks with abstract cityscapes while devouring science‑fiction novels by William Gibson and Neal Stephenson.
info.travel_persona: Brian Keller, a meticulous planner, has explored the modernist streets of Barcelona and the culinary markets of Montreal on solo trips, dreams of wandering Kyoto’s zen gardens and Reykjavik’s aurora‑lit cliffs, and prefers low‑key Airbnb stays that offer quiet workspaces and a kitchen to tend to their herb cuttings.
info.culinary_persona: Brian Keller, an intermediate home cook, cultivates basil, rosemary, and thyme in a small indoor herb garden and frequently crafts pesto‑laden spaghetti, aromatic ratatouille, and miso‑glazed salmon, favoring fresh ingredients like olive oil, garlic, and seasonal vegetables while occasionally treating themselves to artisanal sourdough from a local bakery.

info.persona: Veronica Fabian merges disciplined, routine‑driven heavy‑truck expertise with an energetic, competitive social streak, balancing meticulous workshop order, weekend community service, and a love for Southern music while they occasionally obsess over equipment logs to the point of insomnia.
info.professional_persona: Veronica Fabian, a 47‑year‑old heavy‑vehicle technician, blends deep expertise in diesel engine overhaul, hydraulic and pneumatic systems, and MIG/TIG welding with a rigorously organized workflow; they apply their competitive drive and sociable mentorship style to enforce safety standards and guide apprentices toward Master ASE certification.
info.cultural_background: Veronica grew up in a middle‑class white family in the Appalachian foothills of southeastern Tennessee, near Chattanooga and Marion County. Her upbringing was steeped in Southern traditions that emphasized hard work, self‑reliance, and community involvement. Her parents encouraged practical skills and a straightforward, routine‑oriented outlook, which later guided her choice of a technical trade. She attended a local community college where she studied mechanical technology before entering the heavy‑equipment field. Veronica remains connected to her cultural roots through participation in a local Methodist congregation, attendance at regional festivals, and a respect for the practical, no‑frills values of her community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Veronica enjoys group activities that match her energetic and sociable nature. She is an active member of a local classic‑truck club, attending monthly rides and technical workshops. She loves attending live country music festivals along the Tennessee River and often volunteers in community projects such as Habitat for Humanity builds. On weekends she goes camping and fishing trips with friends, maintains a vegetable garden, and participates in group fitness classes like boot‑camp and indoor cycling. She stays up‑to‑date on automotive trends by reading specialist magazines and enjoys watching regional motorsports events, as well as cooking Southern family‑style meals for gatherings.
info.sports_persona: Veronica Fabian passionately supports the Nashville Predators and the Tennessee Titans while regularly participating in boot‑camp fitness classes, joining the local classic‑truck club’s rally drives, and spending weekends fishing the Tennessee River with a crew they treat each game and outing as a competitive team challenge.
info.arts_persona: Veronica Fabian is an avid follower of live country music festivals, eagerly attending shows featuring Eric Church, Maren Morris, and the Grand Ole Opry, and they also unwind in the garage with classic rock legends such as ZZ Top and Lynyrd Skynyrd, letting the music shape both their social gatherings and repair rhythms.
info.travel_persona: Veronica Fabian prefers meticulously planned road‑trip getaways, having camped in the Great Smoky Mountains, road‑tripped to Austin for South by Southwest, and charted a future journey to New Orleans for its jazz scene, and they ensure each itinerary aligns with work schedules and budget constraints.
info.culinary_persona: Veronica Fabian enjoys cooking Southern comfort meals such as smoked pork ribs, collard greens, and cornbread, often incorporating fresh tomatoes and okra from their garden, and they have a habit of over‑seasoning their chili during community cook‑offs to impress fellow truck enthusiasts.

info.persona: John Tiemann is a meticulous yet laid‑back emergency responder who balances a love for rugged outdoor traditions with a quiet worry about stability, often found tinkering in the garage while plotting the next fishing trip.
info.professional_persona: John Tiemann, a veteran emergency medical technician with over two decades of rapid patient assessment, trauma stabilization, and advanced life‑support expertise, channels their practical, structure‑loving mindset into chaotic emergency scenes while maintaining a relaxed, flexible approach to scheduling, and they mentor new EMTs and lead community first‑aid workshops as they pursue paramedic certification and a senior EMS leadership role.
info.cultural_background: John was raised in a tight‑knit, rural South‑Texas community with German‑Anglo ancestry. He grew up attending a local Baptist church, where service and neighborly support were core values. Family traditions include celebrating Texas Independence Day with a backyard barbecue and fireworks, participating in the Atascosa County Fair, and volunteering with the volunteer fire department. Living in a bilingual region, he learned basic Spanish to communicate with Hispanic neighbors and patients. His cultural outlook emphasizes self‑reliance, modesty, respect for the land, and a strong sense of community responsibility.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, John enjoys spending quiet mornings fishing the Guadalupe River and hunting deer and turkey during the season, activities that connect him to the Texas Hill Country landscape. He is an avid woodworker, crafting furniture and restoring a 1975 Chevrolet truck in his garage. Gardening a small vegetable plot provides a soothing routine, while evenings are often filled with country music, watching the Texas Longhorns, or attending local live‑music gatherings. He also reads mystery novels and keeps up with books on emergency preparedness, reflecting his lifelong curiosity and desire for self‑reliance.
info.sports_persona: John Tiemann enjoys seasonal outdoor pursuits—early‑morning Guadalupe River fishing, deer and turkey hunting with the Hill Country Sportsmen’s Association, and a casual gym routine—while cheering on the Texas Longhorns football team, the San Antonio Spurs, and the Houston Astros, balancing a love of rugged activity with a moderate, health‑focused fitness regimen.
info.arts_persona: John Tiemann channels their creative side through meticulous wood‑craft, all while unwinding to classic country legends like George Strait and Willie Nelson at Gruene Hall and devouring mystery novels by Agatha Christie and Michael Connelly, a blend of hands‑on artistry and storytelling that defines their leisure.
info.travel_persona: John Tiemann prefers low‑key, spontaneous road trips through the Texas Hill Country—visiting wineries in Fredericksburg, live‑music spots in Austin, and the coastal dunes of Padre Island—while dreaming of a rugged adventure in Big Bend National Park, balancing relaxed planning with the occasional overbooking due to unpredictable shift changes.
info.culinary_persona: John Tiemann enjoys cooking hearty Texas fare—smoked brisket, chili with home‑grown tomatoes and peppers, and grilled catfish—leveraging their proficient grill skills and fresh garden harvest, while also indulging in a well‑earned slice of pecan pie after long hunting days.
